character.name: Mr. Thorne
character.personality: Gruff, proud and easily offended, but not cruel. Under the grumbling he is a fair-minded gardener.

knows.fact: Mr. Thorne grows a giant pumpkin called Goliath.
Mr. Thorne has won many blue prize ribbons for his vegetables.

state.demeanor: Prickly and defensive. He has heard he is being blamed and is cross about it.

clues.text: Huge boot prints sink deep into the flower bed outside the broken window, near Mr. Thorne's fence. They are far too big for a child.

gates.says: Mr. Thorne admits he climbed over on Friday at four to measure Bertha through the window, and that the boot prints are his. He says Bertha was perfectly whole.
takes_back: Mr. Thorne says he has never set foot in the school garden.

clues.text: A tall ladder leans on Mr. Thorne's side of the fence, right opposite the greenhouse. A tape measure dangles from its top rung.
Toby says that on Thursday Mr. Thorne was up his ladder, staring at Bertha with a tape measure. Mr. Thorne said, 'Enjoy her while she lasts!'

gates.says: Mr. Thorne says he measured Bertha from his ladder on Thursday, and that 'Enjoy her while she lasts' meant his Goliath would beat her at the weigh-in.

story_so_far.says: Mr. Thorne says he was at the fair all evening with Goliath, at the growers' barbecue from seven till eleven.
Mr. Thorne says that at nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.
Mr. Thorne says he has never set foot in the school garden.

established: Mr. Thorne's ears turn red and he scuffs one huge boot on the grass.
